Description:

Computer animated films are created utilizing digital Animation software. The earliest came in the form of abstract, generated Computer Graphics visuals. However, as the software to create and render 3D visuals improved, feature-length narrative films were able to be produced.

The Mind's Eye [The Mind's Eye: A Computer Animation Odyssey] (1990), and its subsequent sequels, are some of the notable early films to utilize computer software to generate animated films. Toy Story (1995) was the first full-length film to utilize such technology, though it was notably a slow process (taking a full week to render roughly 3 minutes of film). 3D rendered films are a common staple of 21st century Family cinema.
